steps.title: Press the 139434 pins and 139435 holders into the back wall
steps.instruction: Keep the assembled cabinet fixed: top panel (node 1), bottom panel (node 2), side panels (nodes 3 and 21) and the back panel (node 4) stay at their final source positions. As shown in printed step 6, take each 139434 pin (4x, nodes 6, 7, 8, 9) and press it straight into its hole in the back panel at the four positions drawn on the rear face. Then fit each 139435 holder (4x, nodes 11, 13, 15, 17) onto the corresponding pin at the same four locations, pressing it on until it seats against the panel. Work one location at a time and keep fingers clear of the parts as they seat. Do not force a part; if it does not enter squarely, withdraw it slightly, realign it with its hole and press again. The manual gives no torque, turn count or cam rotation for these fittings, so none is shown. This is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: the printed detail shows a bare hand pressing a small fitting into the panel; keep fingers clear of the part and the panel face while pressing.
Do not force a fitting; if it does not enter squarely, withdraw it slightly, realign it with its hole and press again.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure; it does not confirm that any fitting is correctly engaged.
The cabinet body must already be fully assembled and seated from the earlier steps; this animation does not verify those connections.
The large panels are held fixed in this step and must not be moved while the fittings are pressed.

Long-term safety warning from the manual context page: the finished cabinet must be fixed to the wall with the supplied fittings, because a tip-over can cause serious or fatal crushing injury. This is distinct from the fitting step animated here and is not performed by this motion.
uncertainties: Mapping of the illustrated hardware to source nodes is inferred from the printed labels only: 139434 (4x) is mapped to nodes 6, 7, 8, 9 and 139435 (4x) to nodes 11, 13, 15, 17 because those are the only source nodes carrying those labels; the drawing gives no per-part position numbers, so which drawn hole corresponds to which labelled node is not resolved.

Pairing of a 139434 pin with a 139435 holder at each location is inferred from proximity in the source transforms (7 with 11 at parent y about -0.152 to -0.153; 8 with 13 at parent z about -0.152 to -0.153; 9 with 15 at parent y about +0.152 to +0.153; 6 with 17 at parent z about +0.152 to +0.153), not from any printed instruction; inventory order was not used as pair identity.

All eight fittings already sit at their final seated positions in the source model, so the proposed offsets are purely presentation displacements that must return to zero. The manual shows no start distance, hole depth, insertion depth or press travel, so the -0.03 m start offset and the -0.005 m / -0.004 m approach keyframes are invented presentation values only.

The press direction is inferred as parent -X (outboard of the back panel, whose plane is perpendicular to parent X at about x = -0.10 m, with the fittings at x about -0.100 to -0.112 m). The illustration gives a screen-space perspective view only, so the real insertion axis, possible tilt, and any thread or cam engagement are not measured.

The printed page shows only 139434 and 139435 with a hand; the source inventory also contains 141413, 141414, 152650 and 152651 parts. Those are not animated here because no diagram evidence on page 11 shows them, but the page alone does not prove that they are absent from this assembly action.
No torque, turn count, cam-lock rotation, screw tightening sequence or final seating force is proposed, because none of these is readable on the selected page and none is in the source geometry.
The 139435 tracks start at fraction 0.15 to suggest that the holders are fitted after the pins; this ordering is an inference from the drawn sequence of details, not a printed instruction.

Working orientation is not reproduced: the illustration shows the cabinet with the rear face toward the viewer, while the source model keeps every panel in its finished cabinet orientation. No cabinet rotation is animated.

Pure single-axis translation does not model collisions between the fittings and the panel, nor any elastic or cam engagement; the animation may visually pass a part through the panel skin before seating.

Continuity with the tentative prior plan: the large panels (nodes 1, 2, 3, 4, 21) are assumed to be already joined and seated from earlier tentative steps, and are kept at zero offset here. If that context is wrong, the fixed-body assumption for this step is also wrong.

steps.title: Slide top panel onto side panel edge and seat the connector fittings
steps.instruction: Keep the side panel (node 3) in its final position and bring the top panel (node 1) to it horizontally, moving along the parent-coordinate Z direction until the panel edge meets the side panel edge and the protruding connector hardware engages the keyhole slots, as shown in the large drawing and the lower-left detail (left-pointing arrow). Follow the upper-left inset: the fittings must be aligned in their slots as shown on the right; the crossed-out version shows an attempt made with the fittings misaligned and must be avoided. After the panels are pushed together, press the joint down at the corner as shown in the lower-right detail to seat the panels; this downward seating press ends at the panels’ final source positions and is therefore not animated in this step. Do not force the panels; if the fittings do not line up, separate, realign and slide again. Watch the hand positions shown in the detail and keep fingers clear of the closing gap.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: the illustration shows hands on the panel edges while the joint closes; keep fingers out of the closing gap and off the connector fittings.
The upper-left inset explicitly marks a misaligned fitting engagement as wrong (crossed out); engage the fittings in their slots before sliding the panels fully together.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
uncertainties: Mapping of the two illustrated panels: the left panel of the drawing is mapped to side panel node 3 (plane at z ≈ -0.166 m, parent coordinates) and the right, moving panel to top panel node 1 (horizontal panel whose edge overlaps the side panel by geometry), because nodes 1 and 3 are listed as a large-component contact candidate with bounds gap 0.0 m.

The drawing does not identify parts by number, so the mirrored alternative side panel node 21 (the opposite side panel) would fit the same picture equally well; node 3 was chosen arbitrarily among the two symmetric side panels.

The illustrated panels could instead correspond to side panel plus bottom panel (node 2) rather than top panel (node 1); both are equally sized and both are contact candidates with the side panels. This was not resolved from page 8.

Start displacement of 0.05 m along +Z is an inferred presentation offset only; the manual gives no travel distance or start gap, and the direction (+Z, i.e. sliding the top panel in -Z toward the side panel edge) is inferred from the left-pointing arrow in the lower-left detail rather than from measured geometry.

The lower-right detail shows a downward press at the corner; that seating motion is not animated because a single track must end at the final zero offset, and no separate press distance is documented.

Connector hardware visible in the page (cam/dowel fittings such as the 139434, 139435 and 141413 positions in the inventory) is not shown as visible or animated, because the drawing gives no part numbers that can be unambiguously matched to those source nodes.

Panel orientation during assembly (panels drawn upright in the illustration while the source top panel is horizontal in the finished assembly) is not represented; only the join path in parent coordinates is proposed.
No torque, turn count or fastener tightening sequence is proposed, because none is readable on the selected page.

steps.title: Lower the opposite side panel onto the open edge of the two-panel corner
steps.instruction: Keep the already joined panels (nodes 1 and 3) fixed at their final source transforms. As shown by the downward arrow on page 9 step 2, bring the opposite side panel (node 21) straight down onto the open edge of the two-panel corner. Lower it until its mating edge reaches the final source position against the top panel connector edge. Do not force the joint; if the edge does not seat freely, lift the panel slightly, realign it, and lower it again. Keep hands clear of the closing edge.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: keep fingers clear of the closing edge while lowering the panel.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
Do not force the joint; if the fittings do not align, lift the panel, realign it, and lower it again.
The two fixed panels must already be fully seated before this step; this animation does not verify their connection.
uncertainties: Page 9 step 2 has no part numbers. The stationary two-panel body is inherited from the prior proposal as top panel node 1 and side panel node 3; page 9 alone does not confirm that these are the two panels already joined.

The moving large panel is mapped to node 21 ('side panel 35x25 (1)'), the opposite side panel, because it is a large panel that ends in contact with node 1 (large-component contact candidate [1,21], gap 0.0 m) and would complete an open three-sided frame. The drawing does not distinguish node 21 from node 2 (bottom panel, which contacts node 3) or node 4 (back panel, which contacts both 1 and 3), so this mapping is an inference.

Node 1 ('top panel 35x25') is drawn as an upright panel in the existing corner on page 9, while its source transform is horizontal in the finished cabinet. Its correspondence is inferred from the prior step and from its contact with node 21, not from matching illustrated orientation.

Node 3 ('side panel 35x25') is mapped to the other stationary panel of the corner. Because nodes 3 and 21 are symmetric opposite side panels, the assignment of which one is fixed and which one moves is inferred from the prior plan, not proven by the drawing.

The 0.10 m upward start offset is an inferred presentation gap; the manual gives no travel distance. The downward direction is inferred from the arrow as a vertical drop in parent coordinates, but the real assembly may require a different approach path or a tilted insertion.
A pure vertical drop may sweep the moving panel edge through the mating edge region before reaching its final position; collision and connector insertion are not modeled.
No torque, turn count, cam-lock rotation, or fastener tightening sequence is proposed because none of these is readable for this step.
The illustration could instead depict adding the second side panel to a back-and-side subassembly rather than to a top-and-side subassembly; if so, this node mapping and motion are not valid.

steps.title: Slide the thin back panel into the frame groove and seat it
steps.instruction: Hold the three-sided frame (top panel and both side panels) fixed at their final source positions. Pick up the thin sheet and offer it to the open side of the frame as shown on the left of printed step 3, with the edge entering the groove. Follow the middle inset: the sheet must sit in the intended groove as drawn on the left of the inset; the crossed-out version shows the sheet tipped into the wrong slot and must be avoided. Push the sheet steadily along the groove direction (right-hand inset arrow) until its edges are fully seated in the grooves and the panel reaches its final position flush with the frame edge. Work the sheet in gradually and keep hands on the flat faces, clear of the closing grooves. This is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: the fingers in the left detail and the middle inset are close to the grooves; keep fingers out of the groove kerfs while the sheet is fed in.
The middle inset explicitly crosses out a wrong groove/slot engagement; the sheet must be started in the intended groove, not tipped into the adjacent slot.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
Do not force the sheet; if it binds, withdraw it slightly, realign to the groove and feed it again.
The stationary frame panels must already be fully seated from earlier steps; this animation does not verify their connections.
uncertainties: Part identity of the moving sheet is inferred, not printed: source node 4 is labelled back panel and is a thin panel (~0.0025 m thick, largest face perpendicular to parent X), matching the thin sheet on page 9 step 3. Page 9 carries no part numbers.

Source node 2 (bottom panel) is a near-flat outer panel that could also be drawn as a sheet-like part; it is excluded as a moving part per the reviewed evidence and because its final transform is a thick outer bottom panel, but the drawing alone does not settle the identity.

Correspondence of the stationary large panels: node 1 is mapped to the upright top panel of the frame, node 3 to the side panel at parent z ~ -0.158..-0.175 and node 21 to the opposite side panel at parent z ~ +0.158..+0.175, because those three are contact candidates with each other (gaps 0.0 m) and form the open three-sided frame drawn. Nodes 3 and 21 are symmetric, so which is drawn left versus right in the illustration is not resolved.

The back panel final plane is perpendicular to parent X, so the only geometrically admissible insertion is a translation within its own plane (parent Y and/or Z). The illustrated screen-space arrow cannot be mapped to a parent axis with certainty; the proposed path uses parent -Y (insertion from the open bottom side, where node 2 is absent) toward +Y, which is an inference, not a measured path.

The 0.09 m and 0.015 m start/intermediate offsets are invented presentation displacements only; the manual gives no insertion distance, clearance, or groove depth. Real insertion may need a different in-plane direction (e.g. along parent Z between the side panels) or a combined translation plus slight tilt.

Groove geometry, kerf width, friction and cam/dowel engagement (parts such as 139434/139435/141413 in the inventory) are not resolvable from page 9; no torque, turn count or fastener sequence is proposed.
Pure in-plane translation does not model any collision between the sheet edges and the frame panel faces; the animation may pass the sheet through material before seating.

Working orientation is not reproduced: the illustration shows the frame upright in screen space while the source panels are in their finished cabinet orientations; only the parent-coordinate insertion path is proposed, with no cabinet reorientation.

Continuity with the tentative prior plan: nodes 1, 3 and 21 are assumed to be the already-joined panels from the earlier tentative steps, whose seating motion was noted as incomplete; if that context is wrong, this node mapping and the fixed-frame assumption are also wrong.

steps.title: Close the remaining open face with the bottom panel
steps.instruction: Hold the body already built in the previous steps fixed: top panel (node 1), side panel (node 3), thin back panel (node 4) and opposite side panel (node 21) stay at their final source positions. As shown in printed step 4, bring the remaining large panel (node 2) to the last open face of the body from outside it, moving it in the parent -Y direction toward the assembly. Follow the upper-right inset: the fittings must line up in their slots before the panel is closed; do not present the panel at an angle as in the misaligned attempt. Push the panel straight in until its edges and fittings reach the final position flush with the body. Do not force the panel; if it does not line up, withdraw it slightly, realign and push again. Keep hands on the flat faces and clear of the closing edges. This is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: the inset shows a hand at the joint while the panel is brought to the body; keep fingers out of the closing gap and off the fittings.
The upper-right inset shows a misaligned fitting attempt that must be avoided; align the fittings in their slots before pushing the panel fully home.
Do not force the panel; if it binds, withdraw it slightly, realign and push again.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
The panels held fixed (nodes 1, 3, 4, 21) must already be fully seated from earlier steps; this animation does not verify their connections.
Long-term safety warning from the manual context page: the finished cabinet must be fixed to the wall with the supplied fittings, since a tip-over can cause serious or fatal crushing injury.
uncertainties: Part identity of the moving panel is inferred, not printed: page 10 step 4 carries no part numbers. Source node 2 ('bottom panel 35x25') is the remaining large outer panel (0.25 x 0.0228 x 0.34575 m, panel-like) that ends in contact with nodes 3, 4 and 21 at bounds gap 0.0 m, matching a panel that closes the last open face after the thin back panel was inserted in step 3.

Mapping of the fixed body to nodes 1 (top), 3 (side), 4 (thin back) and 21 (opposite side) is inherited from the tentative prior plan and the reviewed evidence, which forbids moving these nodes in this step. Page 10 alone does not label which drawn face is which source panel; nodes 3 and 21 are symmetric so left/right assignment in the drawing is unresolved.

Working orientation is not reproduced: the illustration shows an upright box in screen space, while in the source model the moving panel's finished plane is horizontal at about y = -0.175 m in the parent frame. The illustrated screen-down arrows are therefore not mapped directly to parent -Y; the proposed path follows the geometry (approach from outside the -Y face toward zero offset) rather than the screen-space arrow.

The start offset of 0.15 m along -parent-Y and the intermediate -0.012 m keyframe are invented presentation gaps only; the manual gives no travel distance, clearance or insertion depth. A different approach distance, a slight tilt during insertion, or a short final seating press may be required in reality.

The exact fitting engagement (parts such as 139434, 139435, 141413, 152650, 152651 in the inventory) is not resolvable from page 10; no torque, turn count, cam-lock rotation or screw tightening sequence is proposed, and no hidden connection geometry is assumed.
Pure translation does not model collisions between the incoming panel edges, fittings and the already seated panels; the animation may pass through material before seating.
The illustration could be read as closing the face opposite the drawn front opening rather than the bottom face; if so, the node assignment for the moving panel would need review.

steps.title: Turn the cabinet and seat the joint
steps.instruction: Follow the cabinet-turning arrow and the downward seating detail in printed step 5. This viewer keeps the source model upright and does not animate this operation.
uncertainties: Assistant-authored diagram summary; no AI animation has been accepted for this action. The static 3D view uses tentative source-node mappings and does not demonstrate this operation.

observations: Printed step 6 labels 139434 and 139435, with four repeated pairs. Those labels match source nodes 6,7,8,9 and 11,13,15,17 respectively.
The source locations are on the back at negative parent X. Use source labels and transforms to pair each holder/pin; do not use inventory order as pair identity.
The diagram shows fitting and pressing the two components. No torque or turn count is supplied.
limitations: Prior step 5 is a manual reference; the scene remains in finished source orientation. Do not claim that a physical turn or seating action has been animated.
Exact insert distances and hardware engagement remain unmeasured; keep all inferences explicit.

geometry_review.scope: AABB proximity only, for components at least 0.1 m wide sharing a parent frame, using a 0.02 m threshold. This does not establish mating features, collision-free paths, or correctness.
